title: "Disillusioned" MAHA leader quits as Trump admin's food agenda spoils: Report
gist: Calley Means, a senior advisor to Health Secretary RFK Jr. and co-author of the "MAHA bible" Good Energy, resigned from the White House. The Wall Street Journal reports he was frustrated that food-industry and special interests were stalling MAHA food policy. The White House recently shelved a definition and regulation of ultraprocessed foods and school-meal protein and sugar rules, while the MAHA base is angry about corporate sponsors such as Walmart, UnitedHealth, Anthropic and OpenAI at a recent MAHA summit.

themes.theme: Means resignation and stalled MAHA food agenda

insights.claim: Calley Means, a senior advisor to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., resigned from the Trump administration. His exit post listed Dietary Guidelines reform, psychedelic reform, removing soda from SNAP, removing food dyes, GRAS reform and overhauling government food procurement as policies he helped steer.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Losing a key MAHA advocate lowers the odds of further food-policy changes that would hit packaged food and beverage makers.
insights.quote: I am resigning from the White House with tremendous respect for President Trump and Bobby Kennedy

insights.claim: Sources close to Calley Means told The Wall Street Journal that he grew "disillusioned" and blamed others in the Trump administration for giving the food industry and special interests too much sway over policy. Others in the administration complained that he would not make political concessions.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Suggests the food-industry lobby is winning inside the White House, a relief signal for processed-food companies.

insights.claim: The Wall Street Journal reported that the White House punted on two of RFK Jr.'s food priorities: defining and regulating ultraprocessed foods, and requiring school meals to have more protein and less sugar.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Ultraprocessed-food regulation is on hold, which reduces near-term regulatory risk for packaged-food makers and school-meal suppliers.

themes.theme: MAHA base backlash over corporate ties

insights.claim: A MAHA summit last month drew criticism for corporate sponsors including Walmart, UnitedHealth, Anthropic, OpenAI and Grail, with sponsorship packages reportedly selling for up to $300,000. Many MAHA members felt this betrayed the movement's grassroots nature.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Corporate alignment with MAHA, including by AI labs, carries reputational risk and could split the movement's political base.

insights.claim: At the MAHA summit, RFK Jr. held a fireside chat with Vice President JD Vance and praised the potential of artificial intelligence. MAHA members are increasingly critical of his failure to deliver key priorities and of his apparent embrace of corporate interests.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Shows the HHS agenda shifting toward AI-friendly, corporate-friendly positions, away from hard food regulation.

insights.claim: Calley Means and his sister Casey Means co-wrote Good Energy, called the "MAHA bible." It advises avoiding processed foods, seed oils, fluoride, receipt paper and birth control pills, and has a chapter titled "Trust Yourself, Not Your Doctor."
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Shows the wellness ideology that drives MAHA policy targets such as seed oils and food dyes.

insights.claim: Trump's nomination of Casey Means for surgeon general was abandoned over concerns about her medical qualifications, her positions on vaccines and her promotion of unproven wellness claims.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: This is the second setback for the Means siblings, adding to signs that the MAHA faction's influence is waning.
